activity.notes: Lepidus joined Octavian and Mark Antony in the legally constituted Second Triumvirate in 43 BCE. The triumvirs exercised extraordinary governing authority over the Roman Republic. Lepidus was stripped of his triumviral political power by Octavian after the Sicilian crisis in 36 BCE. ATLAS therefore records a Roman Republic governs + de_facto_rule Activity for 43–36 BCE, reusing the same Triumvir semantics already used for Mark Antony rather than creating the Second Triumvirate as a separate sovereign polity.
